head: d88ae0c6269e067602a90ed8e655df275f6f42f7
summary: INCOMPLETE at exact head d88ae0c6269e067602a90ed8e655df275f6f42f7 (tree feb97fec28afe5f61b69ca0e20ba01662380fdb7), the r4-gated head of fork branch solr-17764-submit. Live verification before and after: fork branch still equals the gated head; PR 5315 head stayed dfde089fd9dd0e5e79774593e66dd030e1b7dd22 (open, not draft). Everything ran in one disposable clone; nothing was pushed and no public comment was made. Environment: Linux, JDK 21, Gradle 9.7.0 via the local wrapper script, seed 17764C0DE, --rerun-tasks. BASELINES at the unchanged head: CloudSolrClientCacheTest 12/12 pass; TestGracefulJettyShutdown 1/1 pass with -Ptests.nightly=true. PROTOTYPE (disposable patch in the evidence archive, 7 files, +887 lines): JettySolrRunner gains ProbeMarkingGracefulHandler (active only under -Dsolr.probe.gracefulMarker=true), a GracefulHandler subclass whose handleShutdownRejection stamps X-Solr-Graceful-Shutdown: probe-5315 before delegating to the stock rejection; a new solrj type GracefulShutdownRejectionException (RemoteSolrException is final, so a subtype was impossible; whether production should use a new type, a marker interface, or un-final RemoteSolrException is an open design question recorded in the patch); both HTTP clients raise it on a 503 carrying the marker (HttpJdkSolrClient in its private processErrorsAndResponse overload; HttpJettySolrClient likewise, closing the response stream first because that path does not parse the body); LBSolrClient catches it ahead of the generic SolrException handling and retries ONLY that subrequest on the next endpoint, without marking the draining endpoint a zombie, and only when isGracefulRejectionRetryable passes: not a V2 request, not UNSPECIFIED type, and not an UpdateRequest carrying a one-shot document iterator. REAL-NODE EVIDENCE (ProbeGracefulRejectionTest, :solr:core:test, 3/3 pass, 0 skipped): on a 1-node MiniSolrCloudCluster with graceful shutdown enabled and the marking handler active, a baseline select returned both docs; an ordinary Solr error (missing collection) produced a plain RemoteSolrException with code 404; two in-flight /foo requests entered the blocking handler (one via CloudSolrClient, one via HttpJettySolrClient); after node stop began, poll 1 was still served and poll 2 received the marked rejection client-side as GracefulShutdownRejectionException; the handler-entry signal proved the rejected request never entered the Solr handler; both in-flight requests then completed with the correct result and the node stopped. The test log's PROBE lines are inside TEST-probe-core.xml in the evidence archive. PLAIN-JETTY CONTROLS (same class): a stock GracefulHandler's shutdown rejection surfaced as an exact-class RemoteSolrException 503 and the wrapped handler was never entered; on a marking server an application-generated 503 stayed an exact-class RemoteSolrException while a post-shutdown request was classified graceful, and an in-flight /slow request completed during the drain. CLIENT/LB EVIDENCE (ProbeGracefulRejectionClientTest, :solr:solrj:test, 6/6 pass, 0 skipped; regressions CloudSolrClientCacheTest 12/12 and LBSolrClientRetryUnsentTest 3/3 also pass): a marked rejection of a materialized atomic-increment UpdateRequest was retried exactly once on the healthy endpoint for BOTH the JDK and Jetty HTTP clients (rejecting endpoint: 1 non-HEAD request, 0 application entries; healthy endpoint: 1 application entry; response status 0). A one-shot document-iterator update was NOT resent (GracefulShutdownRejectionException surfaced; healthy endpoint untouched). An UNSPECIFIED GenericSolrRequest was NOT resent. A V2 request was NOT resent (Jetty client leg; under the test security manager the JDK HttpClient is denied the URLPermission for the header set a V2 request carries, before any I/O). With no alternate endpoint the failure surfaced as SolrServerException caused by GracefulShutdownRejectionException after exactly 1 request, no replay. An unmarked application 503 surfaced as an exact-class RemoteSolrException and was NOT retried. Wire-count note: HttpJdkSolrClient sends a one-time HEAD probe per base URI (HTTP/2 upgrade check, JDK-8287589); the probe was excluded from all counts, and during shutdown that HEAD is itself rejected like any request. PACKAGED SERVER (packaged.log in the archive): :solr:packaging:installDist exit 0 built solr-11.0.0-SNAPSHOT from the probe tree. The distribution ships server/etc/jetty-graceful.xml, which instantiates the STOCK org.eclipse.jetty.server.handler.GracefulHandler on the Jetty start classpath; server/lib holds Jetty jars only and solr-core exists solely under server/solr-webapp/webapp/WEB-INF/lib, so no webapp or solr-core class can be named in that XML. First start attempt on this host never served: in cloud mode the CoreContainer timed out connecting to the embedded ZooKeeper after 15000 ms because the packaged JVM runs without -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true (the bare-JVM loopback trap); every request returned Jetty's default HTML 503 with no marker. With JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS=-Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true the same distribution served normally (collection created, document indexed and returned), and a 200-request loop during bin/solr stop saw only 200s before a clean stop (exit 0); no stock rejection was captured in the window, and none could carry a marker under the stock class. EXACT PRODUCTION PACKAGING CHANGE: place a marking GracefulHandler subclass in a jar on the server start classpath (server/lib or server/lib/ext) and name that class in server/etc/jetty-graceful.xml in place of the stock class; the probe's marking class lives in solr-test-framework, which is not packaged. PRE-EXISTING REPLAY PATHS (requirement 4): UNCHANGED by the prototype. CloudSolrClient still treats RequestNotSentException as a communication error that may replay a whole batch, and the RouteException 503 retry still replays whole requests; the prototype does not map the marker onto either path and adds only the separately guarded LB-subrequest path above. COVERAGE GAPS (why the verdict is incomplete, not passed): (1) The headline two-node/multi-shard CloudSolrClient fan-out was NOT exercised: no real routed batch had one shard complete and another rejected mid-fan-out with persisted atomic increments checked exactly once; the LB evidence uses fake endpoints and a materialized update, and the real-node evidence is a single node with queries, not a routed update. (2) The async path (LBAsyncSolrClient) was not patched or exercised; only sync behavior is proven, although both async-capable HTTP clients share the patched detection code. (3) Mixed-version behavior was covered only by the stock-GracefulHandler control (same Jetty version), not by a real older Solr server. (4) No proxy or header-modifying intermediary was exercised; the supported boundary is a direct node-to-client connection, and the probe establishes no intermediary provenance: an intermediary that strips the header silently disables the optimization, and one that can add the header could forge the signal, so production use must treat the marker as trusted only on direct node connections. (5) The ordinary-503 control on the real node was a 404 error path; real-node application 503s were not separately produced (application 503s were exercised on fake endpoints and the plain-Jetty control). (6) This client version has no ContentStream or streaming update API, so the only non-repeatable body form that exists, the one-shot document iterator, is the one tested. RECOMMENDATION: the real-boundary evidence supports one narrow production change: the start-classpath marking handler above, the dedicated client exception in both HTTP clients, and the guarded LB-subrequest retry exactly as prototyped. The original in-flight indexing case remains unresolved by this design: a request already inside the handler when shutdown begins is not rejected and gets no marker, and SOLR-18341's set/delete classification was not copied or assumed. Executor stop: all Gradle and packaged-server processes from this probe are stopped (verified: no GradleDaemon or start.jar process remains); the disposable clone retains the staged prototype patch and is not pushed anywhere.
